To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The use of the adsorption/thermal-desorption (ATD) technique for the determination of nonpolar trace organic compounds in rain samples has been demonstrated to be effective and reliable.
(1) The design and use of a rain sampler that collects rainwater, filters the rainwater in situ, and concentrates nonpolar organic analytes by adsorption/ thermal desorption is described.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of rain collectors and the application of these collectors for the determination of trace organic compounds in rainwater.

the development of an analytical method for the measurement of trace organic compounds in rainwater, and with the application of that method to the determination of the concentrations of selected nonpolar organic contaminants in rainwater samples collected in the Portland, Or, area.
the determination of the concentrations of trace organic compounds in rain and the use of these concentrations to estimate the local atmospheric concentrations of the compounds at the time of rain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the present study show that the concentrations of the trace organic compounds studied are low, but measurable in rain.
the use of a rain sampler of this type is an effective means for the determination of dissolved concentrations of nonpolar, organic compounds in rainwater.
the use of the adsorption/thermal-desorption (ATD) method for the determination of trace organic compounds in rainwater is feasible, reliable, and useful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a rain collector with a large collection area (0.89 m2) and the use of a Tenax-GC adsorption/thermal-desorption (ATD) cartridge for sample concentration and cleanup has provided the first data for the dissolved concentrations of a variety of trace organic compounds (e.g., polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) and chlorinated hydrocarbons) in rain collected in the Portland, Oregon area.
we developed and tested a new rainwater sampling and analysis system for trace organic contaminants.
we developed and demonstrated a new technique for the determination of trace organic compounds in rain and snow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the ATD technique for the determination of trace organic compounds in rainwater can be recommended.
we need to be more careful with our rainwater collection and analysis, especially for compounds that are known to adsorb to surfaces.
